new_statements.rule_in_words: Buru is reported as a tone language with three level tones (High, Mid, Low). No source says anything about word stress; the tone inventory itself is Blench's reading of Robert Koops's unpublished 1970s wordlist, not a phonological description.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Blench 2016 slides: 'Not much more to say without more data.'
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form wordlist data only (~400 words); no phrase-level or grammatical description exists (Blench 2024 gives 'no data' for word order).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.3 'Buru-Angwe' merges Buru (buru1326, the village east of Baissa) with Angwe (angw1241, Batu Angwe village), which Blench's Atlas (eds. 3 and 4) and Piron still list under the Batu [btu] cluster; Blench 2016 (Tivoid p. 14) moves Angwe to Buru. All data examined concern Buru proper (Koops wordlist); nothing examined describes Angwe separately.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Table 8 'Tone systems in Bantoid and Bantu' (printed p. 24, pdf p. 25) has the row 'Buru | Buru | H, M, L | Koops (ms.)', i.e. three level tones reported second-hand from Koops's unpublished wordlist; other Buru rows: four noun-class prefix pairs, 7 vowels, ATR 'No analysis', word order 'no data'.

sources.note: No descriptive source: all three MEDs are 'wordlist_or_less' (Blench 2006 wordlist; Piron 1996/1997). The five 'glottolog_refs' in WORLD_TARGETS (Nasukawa 2011, Papillon 2020, Kaplan & Zaenen 1989, Choi 1995, Dolatian et al.) are computerized mis-assignments from the trigger word 'precedence' and the sil16 refs are B. D. Grimes's ethnography of Buru (Indonesia) — none concern this language.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Buru–Angwe language' (cites Ethnologue 15, Blench 2019 Atlas ed. 4, Blench 2016 Tivoid p. 14).

Blench, Roger. 2016. The Tivoid languages: overview and comparative wordlist. Paper to accompany a presentation at Bantu VI, Helsinki; circulation draft, 15 September 2016 (Glottolog ref 78922). Section 6.5 Buru, p. 14.
sources.note: Nothing on Buru prosody; 6.5 is classification only ('It is here treated as an isolate within Bantoid'); section 3.3 Tones covers Tiv, Ugarə and Esimbi, not Buru.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2016. Tivoid. Slides, Bantu VI, Helsinki, June 2016 (slide 'Is Buru Tivoid?').
sources.note: Nothing on stress; 'Buru is known only from about 400 words collected by Robert Koops in the 1970s... Unusual phoneme /θ/... Not much more to say without more data.'

sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone system; only 'Phonologically, Buru has several unusual features, including the voiceless dental /θ/... Cr clusters and more unusual sequences such as θb and tθ' (p. 21) plus a table of tone-marked lexemes (level tone diacritics on e.g. ēbum/ābúm) and the noun-class pairings; states the only data is Koops's 1970s manuscript wordlist.
